page: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Haswell processor running at 2.0 GHz with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, operating without hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 15.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, alongside a 100 GB local SSD. Network connectivity is defined by a 0 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the older Intel Haswell architecture delivers modest processing power. Single-core stress-ng performance falls into the bottom 10%, while multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench scores reside in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; small-block cached read bandwidth is average, but large-block uncached read and write speeds are weak. Database operations and text processing achieve average marks, whereas Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput are positioned in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the b2-15 instance is the provision of dedicated physical cores at the expense of modern architectural efficiency and raw compute speed. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a balanced allocation of memory and local SSD storage for utility workloads without the premium of high-performance silicon. This profile is best suited for general-purpose tasks, lightweight database operations, basic web serving, and development environments that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high-throughput processing or rapid memory bandwidth.
